ATE and CATE estimate treatment effects; MCAR, MAR, and MNAR assumptions guide handling incomplete data.

C-statistic (AUC) measures discrimination: probability a case ranks higher than a control. Pair discrimination with overall performance metrics such as Brier score = mean((p - y)^2), where lower values indicate better probabilistic accuracy. AUC can be unstable in small or imbalanced samples, so include calibration checks and uncertainty estimates.
Credible intervals contain the true parameter with the stated posterior probability. Computed via posterior quantiles (e.g., qnorm(0.975) for an N(0,1) posterior).
Intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) = between-group variance / total variance; quantifies clustering in random-intercept models. Values near 1 indicate most variability is between groups.

Bonferroni divides alpha by the number of tests (alpha/m) for strict family-wise error rate control. Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) controls FDR by comparing ranked p-values to (k/m)*q thresholds; less conservative than Bonferroni and preferred when many tests are conducted.

Propensity score matching (PSM) estimates the ATT by matching treated units to controls with similar propensity scores. ATT = mean outcome (treated) - mean outcome (matched controls). Balances observed confounders but not unobserved ones.

Net benefit (NB) = TP/N - (FP/N) * (pt/(1-pt)) where pt is the decision threshold probability. DCA plots NB across thresholds to compare clinical utility of prediction models versus treat-all / treat-none strategies.
